Except that back when Windows first came up, you didn't had to download a new version of your programs each time you wanted to use them, and you were not forced to hand out private data to suspicious third-parties.

HTML5 being the new Windows implies that HTML5 is even close to as standardized as Windows is. Which it's not. At the bleeding edge there are still loads of incompatibilities between browsers. This causes all kinds of application development problems. Not all of these incompatibilities can be polyfilled or worked around. Some things just plain will not work without browser support. Sometimes things work for a while and then an update is released for a particular browser that completely breaks a core piece of your application's functionality. That's fun to explain to clients. With OS updates they were big enough, infrequent enough, and required enough effort to install that people understood that something could break. No one looks at browsers the same way and their updates are frequent.
It's shit like that why I prefer desktop development to web development.
